purpose: Element fidelity over a magicbrush-style edit corpus: short single-clause instructions over real photographs. Change/preserve authored separately so under-edit and over-edit fail different halves.
authoring_note: The BEFORE images are arbitrary real photographs from the magicbrush corpus, so `preserve` items are deliberately global-consistency questions (identity, composition, untouched regions, photographic register) rather than named background objects — an author who has not seen every before image must not invent scene detail. `change` items are specific, because the instruction fully determines them. This asymmetry is the honest one: compliance is crisply checkable, preservation is checked as 'nothing else moved'.

edit.instruction: let the skateboard read JESUS

change.question: In the after image, does the skateboard carry the readable word JESUS on it?

preserve.question: Is the skateboard the same shape and in the same position in both images?
Apart from the lettering on the skateboard, is the rest of the scene unchanged between the two images?
Is the after image still a photograph in the same style and lighting as the before image?

edit.instruction: Put a plate under the pancakes.

change.question: In the after image, is there a plate underneath the pancakes that was not there before?
Are the pancakes actually resting on top of that plate, rather than the plate floating or overlapping them?

preserve.question: Are the pancakes themselves unchanged in number, shape and appearance?
Apart from the added plate, is the rest of the scene unchanged between the two images?
Is the after image still a photograph in the same style and lighting as the before image?

preserve.question: Is the teddy bear unchanged in appearance and position between the two images?
Apart from the added doll, is the rest of the scene unchanged between the two images?
Is the after image still a photograph in the same style and lighting as the before image?

Is the after image still a photograph in the same style and lighting as the before image?
